scope: Exact-firmware auxiliary track-location classification and host fixes; corrected runtime remains untested

source_facts.fact: Packs a 36-byte TrackLocation from native MediaID and content ID. Validity is byte 0; MediaID kind byte 1, zero-based member byte 2, media kind/subkind bytes 3/4, track type byte 5; content ID occupies bytes 8..11.

Existing exact-media construction uses low 16 bits 2 | ((player - 1) << 8). Together with the captured little-endian MediaID component bytes, row kind 2/member index 6 or 7 identifies private players 7 or 8.
Native empty TrackLocation constructor clears all 36 bytes, including validity.
Serializes TrackLocation through 0x1041330, resolving local-member identity when necessary.
Writes ten auxiliary TrackLocation records at payload offset 0x168 + 0x40*i, i=0..9. Status wire payload begins at 0x24, giving wire rows 0x18c + 0x40*i.
Writes another TrackLocation at payload offset 0x404, giving wire row 0x428.

classification_of_previous_marker.classification: Content ID of the first auxiliary TrackLocation, independent of the current standard source tuple.
classification_of_previous_marker.conclusion: The first auxiliary row explicitly exposes private member 7 and content 495 in every observed packet, including packets whose standard source tuple was already masked.

implementation: hub_status_hide_private_locations checks exact 1152-byte status framing and examines all eleven known location rows independently of packet sender/current source.
Only valid rows with MediaID kind 2 and member index 6/7 are replaced by the native 36-zero-byte empty location.
All other bytes, surrounding cue/transport data, preference rows and native/external locations with identical content IDs are preserved.
The cached-status classifier optionally uses committed successful-load origin independently of mutable pending load data or physical source presence.

Committed private origin requires nonzero controller/media/epoch, matching deck/content, private source index and a complete saved physical connection identity. Pending/failure keeps it; native/external success or real unload retires it through generator callback integration.
